title: AI UGC Video Ads for TikTok and Reels | AIVideosUGC
description: Create AI UGC video ads with a casual creator-style look from a product photo. Download the clip and add captions in TikTok, Reels, or Facebook.
h1: AI UGC Video Ads With a Casual, Creator-Style Look
lead: Make short UGC-style video ads for TikTok, Reels and Shorts from one product photo. The person in the video is AI-generated, so show the product and explain a real feature instead of presenting a fake review. Build a focused scene that gives a shopper a reason to keep watching.

steps.d: Upload a well-lit photo with the whole product in frame, including color and details the presenter must hold or demonstrate.
Name one setting and action, then choose a configured frame such as 9:16 for TikTok and Reels.
Download the scene, check the presenter and product, then type the headline, price or offer in your editor.

faq.q: What should I write in the description?
faq.a: One everyday moment with your product in it. Name the place, the light, and the action, for example “sunny bathroom counter, hand picks up the soap bar and turns it.” Keep it to a single scene so the clip stays focused. For a product demo, name the first frame and the last frame so the action has a clear finish.

faq.q: Can I present an AI-generated person as a real customer?
faq.a: No. The person and scene are AI-generated; they are not customer footage or a real endorsement. Use disclosure language that your platform and local rules accept.

faq.q: Can I add captions, a price, or music?
faq.a: Yes, once the clip is downloaded. Captions and music go on in TikTok or CapCut, and prices or discount codes can be added in CapCut or Ads Manager. Typing text yourself avoids the spelling slips that AI-made lettering can have. Export a clean master first, then add channel-specific text and sound.

faq.q: Can I make a product demonstration ad?
faq.a: Yes. Start with a clear product reference and describe one believable action a customer can understand. Show the product before the presenter changes pose.

faq.q: Can I choose a square or vertical output?
faq.a: Yes. The available video size choices include 9:16, 1:1, 16:9 and other configured ratios. Pick the frame that matches the placement, then confirm its crop in the editor.

faq.q: How many credits does a video ad cost?
faq.a: A 6-second clip costs 24 credits, a 10-second clip 40 credits and a 15-second clip 60 credits. The editor shows the cost before you generate. The credit total is shown before you submit, so test a shorter version first.

faq.q: How do I keep an AI presenter honest?
faq.a: Use a brand-led explanation or a real, approved customer quote. Identify the person as AI-generated where required, avoid invented experience, and make sure every product benefit can be supported by your own listing or testing. Keep the wording tied to a supported product detail and avoid claims about personal results.

faq.q: What should the first seconds show?
faq.a: Show the product and the problem or action immediately: a hand opens the cap, clears a sofa stripe, or lifts the shoe. A single visible action gives the viewer context before the spoken hook or caption appears. Keep the first shot legible even on a small phone screen.

overview.h2: Keep the product at the center of a casual scene
overview.p: A casual scene can show a product in an ordinary moment, such as packing a lunch bag or picking up a speaker. The person and setting are AI-generated.

examples.lead: See how creators can demonstrate products with a try-on, an unboxing, a routine or a clear before-and-after. Each format gives the presenter one visible job so the scene can support a specific hook in a paid placement.

uses.d: Creator-led vertical ads fit naturally in short-form social feeds. Open with the product in hand, keep the useful action close, and add captions in the platform editor so the claim is readable when audio is off. Place the product in the first frame and repeat the key detail in captions.

Creator-led ads give you a clear place to test hooks while keeping the product in view. Change one opening line or action at a time, then compare watch-through and clicks for that offer. Keep the hook change small so the watch-through difference has a clear reason.
